questions_for_integrator: Does the 3.5 cm wheel radius reduce line_loss_events below 1.0 per run on the s-bend and slalom?
At what progress does the first line loss occur now, and is max_error at the 0.06 m limit before or after it?
Does steering_oscillation rise with the larger radius (above about 0.2 would suggest overshoot)?
Do the wheels slip on starts, and does completion_time approach 3 s on any track?

intent: Test a single turn-authority change against iteration 3: raise wheel_radius from 0.03 to 0.035 m with everything else unchanged. A larger radius gives more yaw rate for the same wheel-speed difference and more ground speed, which should cut line loss on the bends and move completion_time toward 3 s. Expected result: line_loss_events at or below 0.5 per run on the s-bend and slalom, max_error below 0.06 m, and progress above the iteration 3 values (oval 0.11, s-bend 0.1275, slalom 0.0975).
learning: If line loss falls, turn authority was the limit and the next step is to tune wheel_track or mass against it. If line loss stays at 1.0 with a larger radius, wheel-speed turn authority is not the cause either, so the next test should look at the start or at a fixed point on the course where all sensors lose the line.
rationale: Across iterations 0 to 3, line_loss_events stayed at about 1.0 per run whatever the sensor span (4 cm or 6 cm), forward offset (0.05, 0.04 or 0.03 m) or mass (0.8, 0.7 or 0.6 kg) was. Steering oscillation stayed low (0.07 to 0.14), so the robot is not jittering. It loses the line once per run and every run still leaves the track at the 0.06 m limit. The most recent change, mass 0.7 to 0.6 kg, lowered the score from 47.85 to 46.16 with no reduction in line loss, so it did not help. Integration feedback rule (3) applies: when line loss persists after sensing and mass changes, the next lever is turn authority, not sensing. Wheel_radius sets how much wheel-speed difference becomes yaw rate: for the same PWM difference, a larger radius gives more yaw rate per metre of track, and it also raises ground speed, which helps the 3 s finish target. I therefore change only wheel_radius, from 0.03 to 0.035 m, against iteration 3. Sensors (y 0.03 m, plus or minus 3 cm span, 16 mm), wheel_track 0.14 m and mass 0.6 kg stay fixed so the result is attributable to the wheel change. Expected result: line_loss_events fall toward 0.5 or less on the s-bend and slalom, max_error stays under 0.06 m, and completion_time falls. This is a hypothesis, not a measured result. If line loss still stays at 1.0, the next test is a wheel_track change (0.16 m), since the sensing has now been varied three times with no effect.
